studyHoursVsStress.title: Study Hours vs. Stress Score
studyHoursVsStress.finding: Average stress increases steadily as independent daily study hours exceed 4 hours per day.
studyHoursVsStress.insight: High study volume without strategic recovery intervals or breaks creates cognitive fatigue, compounding academic strain.

attendanceVsStress.title: Class Attendance vs. Stress Score
attendanceVsStress.finding: Students maintaining >85% attendance experience significantly lower average stress scores (60.1 vs 71.5 for <60%).
attendanceVsStress.insight: Consistent attendance reduces lecture backlogs and anxiety surrounding unlearned material and impending assessments.

examFrequencyVsStress.title: Exam Frequency vs. Stress Score
examFrequencyVsStress.finding: A non-linear stress spike occurs when exam density exceeds 4 major exams in a single academic term.
examFrequencyVsStress.insight: Frequent high-stakes examinations create continuous performance pressure with insufficient recovery periods.

assignmentLoadVsStress.title: Assignment Load vs. Stress Score
assignmentLoadVsStress.finding: Submitting 5 or more weekly assignments correlates with an average 19.4 point increase in stress.
assignmentLoadVsStress.insight: Fragmented and overlapping deadlines prevent deep learning and disrupt sleep schedules.

sleepVsStress.title: Sleep Hours vs. Stress Score
sleepVsStress.finding: Students averaging <5 hours of sleep report a severe average stress score of 75.4, compared to 52.8 for >8 hours.
sleepVsStress.insight: Sleep deprivation impairs emotional regulation and prefrontal executive function, amplifying perceived difficulty of academic tasks.

screenTimeVsStress.title: Screen Time vs. Stress Score
screenTimeVsStress.finding: Screen time exhibits a strong linear upward relationship with student stress (r = 0.420, p < 0.001).
screenTimeVsStress.insight: Excessive screen immersion displaces physical movement and restorative offline socializing while increasing blue-light melatonin inhibition.

socialMediaVsStress.title: Social Media Use vs. Stress Score
socialMediaVsStress.finding: Students spending >4 hours daily on social media score 17.2 points higher in stress than those with <1 hour.
socialMediaVsStress.insight: Algorithmic feed consumption triggers social comparison loops, FOMO, and cognitive fragmentation.

anxietyVsStress.title: Anxiety Level vs. Stress Score
anxietyVsStress.finding: Anxiety is the single strongest positive predictor of university stress (r = 0.510, R² = 0.260).
anxietyVsStress.insight: Baseline generalized anxiety lowers psychological resilience thresholds, causing minor academic events to trigger acute stress reactions.

familySupportVsStress.title: Family Support vs. Stress Score
familySupportVsStress.finding: High family emotional and logistical support serves as an essential protective buffer, reducing stress by 13.4 points.
familySupportVsStress.insight: Validating familial environments provide emotional safety valves that prevent academic anxiety from spiraling.

peerPressureVsStress.title: Peer Pressure vs. Stress Score
peerPressureVsStress.finding: Competitive peer pressure environments elevate subjective academic tension and imposter phenomenon.
peerPressureVsStress.insight: Grade-sharing and competitive benchmarking between classmates exacerbate anxiety over relative academic standing.

genderVsStressLevel.title: Gender vs. Stress Level Distribution
genderVsStressLevel.description: 100% Stacked categorical distribution of stress severity across gender categories.
genderVsStressLevel.finding: Female students report a slightly higher prevalence of High and Very High stress (42.5% vs 35.8% for Male).
genderVsStressLevel.insight: Potential factors include differential willingness to report psychological distress and uneven domestic/care responsibilities.

tuitionVsStressLevel.title: Tuition Funding vs. Stress Level Distribution
tuitionVsStressLevel.description: 100% Stacked distribution comparing financial tuition structures against stress severity.
tuitionVsStressLevel.finding: Self-funded and student loan cohorts display a 48.2% combined high stress rate vs 31.4% for scholarship holders.
tuitionVsStressLevel.insight: Financial precarity creates concurrent off-campus work obligations, directly eroding available study and sleep windows.

universityTypeVsStressLevel.title: University Type vs. Stress Level Distribution
universityTypeVsStressLevel.description: 100% Stacked distribution evaluating institutional type impact on stress levels.
universityTypeVsStressLevel.finding: Private university cohorts exhibit statistically significant elevated stress (p = 0.007, F = 5.02).
universityTypeVsStressLevel.insight: Higher tuition stakes, intensive grading curves, and networking expectations contribute to elevated baseline pressure.
